title: Online bullying rising again; Kids using AI to humiliate each other, teachers
source_used: NL Times, citing RTL Nieuws, which relays figures from Offlimits
key_facts: Offlimits, the expertise centre for online abuse, reported on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that online bullying is rising again; RTL Nieuws also reported it.
Between January and September 2026 Offlimits received 955 reports of online bullying or abuse, compared with 860 in the whole of 2025 and 298 in 2024.
AI-generated or manipulated images account for 17.4% of the reports, up from 2% in 2024.
Young people report that peers use AI to make fake images showing them kissing, dancing or vomiting; some images also involve teachers.
For children from some religious backgrounds, fake images showing them dancing or kissing can have serious consequences.
Offlimits urges parents and schools to talk with children about online behaviour, starting at an early age.
